original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence-algebra}
Let $R \to A \to B$ be ring maps.
Assume $R \to B$ is of finite presentation and
$A \to B$ faithfully flat and of finite presentation.
Then $R \to A$ is of finite presentation.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $R\to A\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. If $B$ is finitely presented as an $R$-algebra and $A\to B$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented, then $A$ is finitely presented as an $R$-algebra.
stage_b_review_note: Retains fpqc descent of finite presentation of R→A from R→B under A→B faithfully flat and finitely presented. Both finiteness hypotheses and ring-map direction preserved.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $R\to A\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. If $B$ is finitely presented as an $R$-algebra and $A\to B$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented, then $A$ is finitely presented as an $R$-algebra.
hypotheses: R→B is finitely presented; A→B faithfully flat and finitely presented.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-local-source-fppf-algebra}
Let $R \to A \to B$ be ring maps.
Assume $R \to B$ is of finite type and
$A \to B$ faithfully flat and of finite presentation.
Then $R \to A$ is of finite type.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $R\to A\to B$ be ring homomorphisms. If $B$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra and the map $A\to B$ is faithfully flat and of finite presentation, then $A$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra.
stage_b_review_note: Retains finite TYPE descent along A→B faithfully flat and finitely presented, with R→B finite type; conclusion is R→A finite type, not stronger finite presentation.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $R\to A\to B$ be ring homomorphisms. If $B$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra and the map $A\to B$ is faithfully flat and of finite presentation, then $A$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra.
hypotheses: R→B finite type; A→B faithfully flat and finite presentation.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation. If $p:X\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, then $q:Y\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. Separately, if $p$ is locally of finite type, then $q$ is locally of finite type.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves geometric descent of locally finite presentation and locally finite type along surjective flat lfp f:X→Y in a composite X→Y→S, with each alternative property of p descending to q.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation. If $p:X\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, then $q:Y\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. Separately, if $p$ is locally of finite type, then $q$ is locally of finite type.
hypotheses: f surjective flat locally finitely presented; p locally finite presentation/finite type.
conclusions: q has the same corresponding finiteness property.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. In each of the following three cases, assume $f$ is surjective and has the indicated property, and $p$ has the same property: (i) both $f$ and $p$ are syntomic; (ii) both are smooth; (iii) both are étale. Then in the corresponding case $q$ is syntomic, smooth, or étale, respectively.
stage_b_review_note: Retains three corresponding cases for surjective syntomic/smooth/étale f:X→Y with composite p:X→S having the SAME property. Y→S inherits that property in each case.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. In each of the following three cases, assume $f$ is surjective and has the indicated property, and $p$ has the same property: (i) both $f$ and $p$ are syntomic; (ii) both are smooth; (iii) both are étale. Then in the corresponding case $q$ is syntomic, smooth, or étale, respectively.
hypotheses: f is surjective, and f and p are both syntomic, or both smooth, or both étale.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. If $f:X\to Y$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation and $p:X\to S$ is smooth, then $q:Y\to S$ is smooth. Under the same assumption on $f$, if $p$ is étale, then $q$ is étale. No smoothness or étaleness conclusion is asserted about $f$.
stage_b_review_note: Retains fpqc-style descent of smoothness and separately étaleness of q:Y→S when f:X→Y is surjective flat lfp and p=q∘f has the desired property. No requirement f smooth or étale.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. If $f:X\to Y$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation and $p:X\to S$ is smooth, then $q:Y\to S$ is smooth. Under the same assumption on $f$, if $p$ is étale, then $q$ is étale. No smoothness or étaleness conclusion is asserted about $f$.
hypotheses: f surjective flat lfp; p smooth or étale.
conclusions: q is correspondingly smooth or étale.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. Assume $f:X\to Y$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation and the composite $p:X\to S$ is syntomic (flat, locally finitely presented, with local complete intersection fibres). Then both $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ are syntomic.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves both syntomic conclusions under f:X→Y surjective flat lfp and p=q∘f syntomic: not only q:Y→S syntomic but f:X→Y syntomic too. The source's lci-fibre characterization is explanatory.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. Assume $f:X\to Y$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation and the composite $p:X\to S$ is syntomic (flat, locally finitely presented, with local complete intersection fibres). Then both $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ are syntomic.
hypotheses: f surjective flat lfp, and p syntomic.
conclusions: Both q and f are syntomic.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-curiosity}
Let $X \to Y \to Z$ be morphism of schemes.
Let $P$ be one of the following properties of morphisms of schemes:
flat, locally finite type, locally finite presentation.
Assume that $X \to Z$ has $P$ and that $\{X \to Y\}$
can be refined by an fppf covering of $Y$. Then $Y \to Z$ is $P$.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q Z$ be morphisms of schemes. Let $\mathcal P$ be one of: flat, locally of finite type, or locally of finite presentation. Suppose $X\to Z$ has $\mathcal P$ and the singleton family $\{X\to Y\}$ admits an fppf refinement: there is an fppf covering $\{U_i\to Y\}$ for which every map $U_i\to Y$ factors through $X\to Y$. Then $Y\to Z$ has $\mathcal P$.
stage_b_review_note: Retains condition that singleton {X→Y} admits an FPPF refinement U_i→Y with each U_i→Y factoring through X→Y. Under p:X→Z flat, locally finite type or locally finite presentation, Y→Z inherits same property.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q Z$ be morphisms of schemes. Let $\mathcal P$ be one of: flat, locally of finite type, or locally of finite presentation. Suppose $X\to Z$ has $\mathcal P$ and the singleton family $\{X\to Y\}$ admits an fppf refinement: there is an fppf covering $\{U_i\to Y\}$ for which every map $U_i\to Y$ factors through $X\to Y$. Then $Y\to Z$ has $\mathcal P$.
hypotheses: X→Z has one of three listed properties, and the family {X→Y} is refined by an fppf cover of Y.
